interpretation: Dynamic-top boundary construction is not the RM14 blocker: the provider is available, finite and physically interpretable at all tested origins/windows.
The exact frozen 8.64-second raw Reference-Richards solve converges before any transaction temporal gate is applied.
Therefore RM14's first 8.64-second transaction rejection occurs after a converged raw solve, in temporal-certificate construction/evaluation.

The transaction retry mechanism then halves the attempt duration; those shorter attempts enter a different regime in which the raw nonlinear solve itself fails. This explains the mixed RM14/RM15 pattern of temporal and solver rejections.
A smaller coupling timestep is not a remedy: RM15 and RM16 show the full 8.64-second raw solve succeeds while shorter raw solves fail.
excluded_hypotheses: invalid dynamic-top sign convention at the accepted origin
runoff/ponding activation causing the first failure
outer physical window simply being too large
next_required_boundary: Isolate temporal-certificate construction on the converged 8.64-second dynamic-top solve. Determine why the Reference temporal indicator is unavailable for that valid solve and whether the missing authority is predecessor/right-derivative state, dynamic boundary derivative support, or another certificate input. Do not change the solve, retry policy or temporal budget.
